subject: MAP: Concurrency thresholds, long-context acceptance & performance benching
messages:
From: Jonathan Reed <jonathan.reed@acmehealth.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP request: performance acceptance criteria & close timeline

Diego,

Thanks for taking this on. Procurement at Acme Health needs a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that includes performance acceptance criteria and an evaluation plan we can share across engineering and compliance. High level asks:

- Acceptance targets (what we care about):
  - Latency: p95 < 80ms for typical patient-facing prompts (avg prompt ~1.2k tokens)
  - TTFT (time-to-first-token): < 300ms for cold requests
  - Throughput: sustain 200 req/s for 90% of business hours
  - Concurrency: support bursts to 256 concurrent sessions without SLA impact
  - Long-context: support up to 65k token sequences for chart ingestion use-cases

- Evaluation plan: test matrix that covers prompt size distribution (short/medium/long), max sequence stress, and KV cache warm/cold behavior. We also need clear pass/fail criteria per test and artifacts (csv of metrics, harness configs).

Timeline: procurement would like to close within three weeks if the MAP and initial bench results look good.

Can you send a proposed MAP with milestones and an initial perf run plan by EOD Wednesday? We can share with our infra team after that.

Attaching the Acme MAP template for your reference.

Thanks,
Jonathan
Jonathan Reed
Director, AI Platforms
Acme Health

Attachment: Acme_MAP_Request.pdf (PDF, 128KB)

From: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Jonathan Reed <jonathan.reed@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-21T13:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP request: performance acceptance criteria & close timeline

Jonathan —

Appreciate the clear asks. Draft MAP + evaluation plan attached and summarized below. High-level plan (two-week experimental window + rollout):

1) Week 1 — Discovery & config
   - Finalize test dataset (we'll synthesize chart prompts + 30% real anonymized prompts).
   - Confirm prompt distribution: short (<512 tokens): 50%, medium (512-4k): 35%, long (4k-65k): 15%.
   - Define sequence buckets: 512, 2k, 8k, 16k, 32k, 65k.

2) Week 2 — Benchmark runs + validation
   - Run controlled bench matrix across: concurrency levels [1, 8, 32, 64, 128, 256], model variants [fp16, int8/quant], with/without KV cache warm.
   - Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, TTFT, tokens/sec, errors, GPU util, peak memory, failure modes.
   - Acceptance gates: p95 latency < 80ms OR documented tradeoffs with recommended config; TTFT < 300ms when KV cache warm for typical prompts; peak memory < node limit for 65k seqs.

3) Post-run — Deliverables
   - CSV of run metrics, MAP-Acme-v1.xlsx (milestones + responsibilities), perf-results-YYYYMMDD.csv, harness-config.yaml.

4) Canary & close
   - 10% canary (dedicated pool) for 48–72h, then 50%/100% ramp if stable.
   - Proposed close target: 2026-05-12 (three weeks) pending results.

We will provide a reproducible test harness and the raw artifacts so Acme can re-run if needed. Marcus will run the first smoke runs on our dedicated cluster today and share initial numbers.

Doc sign/e-sign ready once MAP milestones are agreed: https://redwood-docsign.example.com/s/DEAL-ACME-00421

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment: MAP-Acme-v1.xlsx (XLSX, 85KB)

From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-22T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Concurrency thresholds, long-context acceptance & performance benching

Quick status — ran the first automated bench against a dedicated 8xA100 pool (config: fp16, batch size auto, KV cache enabled/disabled per test). Key observations (smoke run):

- Short prompts (<=512 tokens) at concurrency 64: p95 latency 42ms, TTFT 95ms (KV cache warm).
- Medium prompts (~2k tokens) at concurrency 64: p95 latency 78ms, TTFT 210ms (KV cache warm).
- Long prompts (32k tokens) at concurrency 16: p95 latency 420ms, TTFT 1.1s (cold); with KV cache warm and prefix caching we observed TTFT drop to ~360ms but P95 still above 300ms for the longest sequences.
- Throughput: sustained ~220 req/s for mixed distribution at concurrency 64 with batching; without batching throughput dropped ~30%.
- Max seq 65k: triggered OOM on node with default memory limits; we hit memory pressure on KV store and had to reconfigure allocation. With larger heap/node config we can run 65k but at reduced concurrency (~8).
- KV cache impact: warm cache reduced TTFT by ~40–55% on average for short/medium prompts; long sequences see less proportional benefit but reduced total token decode work for re-used prefixes.

Attached raw CSV and harness config. Next steps: run full sweep (1/8/32/64/128/256) and both quantized fp16 and int8 profiles. I'll add recommended node-sizing for 65k sequences in the report.

--Marcus
Marcus Lin
Performance Engineering Lead | Redwood Inference

Attachments: perf-results-20260421.csv, harness-config.yaml

- Put explicit acceptance fallback: if 65k sequences cannot hit p95 < 300ms at any cost-effective node size, we need an agreed operational mitigation (shard sequences or hybrid approach) documented in the MAP.
- Confirm procurement gating: DocuSign only after the 48h canary (we will not sign to production until canary is green).

Tessa -- can you schedule a 30-min closure call on Friday to sync on procurement timelines and responsibilities? I'll bring the recommended mitigations for long sequences.

Grace O'Connor
Director, Product | Redwood Inference

Jonathan —

- Marcus: complete full bench sweep (concurrency matrix + quant profiles) by 2026-04-25. Deliver: perf-results-20260425.csv and updated harness-config.yaml.
- Diego (me): finalize MAP and send for internal DocuSign pre-approval by 2026-04-26.
- Grace: approve mitigation language and sign-off on canary checklist by 2026-04-26.
- Tessa: schedule closure call Friday 2026-04-24 10:00 PT (inv sent).

Acceptance summary (short):
  - Primary pass: p95 < 80ms for short/medium distribution at target throughput; TTFT < 300ms when KV cache warm for typical prompts.
  - Long sequence (>=32k): documented acceptable tradeoffs and mitigation plan; canary must demonstrate safe operation at expected job mix.

We'll share the full artifacts once Marcus completes the sweep. If anything slips on the timeline I'll flag immediately.

Regards,
Diego Fernandez
